subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should the public web-tool egress boundary be for domain allow/deny controls: a scoped web_fetch policy, a cross-tool search/fetch/browser policy, or managed-proxy-owned egress?
rationale: This adds an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the open related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while keeping denied domains, search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Design Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Pause narrow local knobs and define one cross-tool contract for fetch, search, browser, providers, plugins, redirects, caches, and proxy routing before implementation lands.

options.title: Use Managed Proxy As Boundary
options.body: Route application-owned egress policy through proxy.enabled and external operator policy instead of adding a local domain firewall to web tools.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while keeping denied domains, search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across SSRF, guarded fetch, web_fetch runtime, and docs touched by this boundary choice.
